title: Balanced Incomplete Block Designs and Incidence Matrices
breadcrumb: Unit III · Design of Experiments · Incomplete block designs
objectives: Define BIBD parameters v, b, r, k and λ.
Construct and interpret the v×b incidence matrix.
Distinguish necessary parameter conditions from existence.

prereq.name: Complete block designs
prereq.why: BIBDs extend blocking when a block cannot contain every treatment.

prereq.name: Matrix multiplication
prereq.why: NN′ records replications and pair concurrence.

prereq.name: Combinatorial counting
prereq.why: The identities count placements and pairs.

mastery.note: Platform settings, not an NTA rule. Ten items are drawn with a 3/5/2 difficulty mix; retakes draw again.

traps: r counts blocks containing one treatment; k counts treatments per block.
λ counts blocks containing a fixed pair, not one treatment.
bk=vr counts placements in two ways.
λ(v−1)=r(k−1) fixes one treatment and counts its partners.
Integer identities are necessary, not sufficient, for existence.
howto: Write v,b,r,k,λ and their meanings. Check bk=vr and λ(v−1)=r(k−1). Build N with treatments as rows and blocks as columns; row sums are r and column sums k. Check NN′: diagonal r, off-diagonal λ.

sheet: v treatments; b blocks; r blocks per treatment.
k treatments per block; λ blocks containing each pair.
λ(v−1)=r(k−1) counts partners of a fixed treatment.
N is v×b: treatments in rows, blocks in columns.
Row sums r; column sums k.
Necessary identities do not prove existence.

tricks.why: It meets v−1 others, each λ times.

shortcuts: Check bk=vr first; both sides count ones in N.
NN′ diagonal entries are r; off-diagonal entries are λ.
remember: Every pair occurs together in exactly λ blocks.
N verifies replication, block size and pair balance.

provenance: Original GPT-authored lesson for design-t4. No official PYQ is claimed. The incidence-matrix example and parameter identities are checked in verify_design_t4.py. Scope: BIBD parameters, incidence matrices, pair concurrence and necessary feasibility identities; connectedness and efficiency are reserved for design-t8.

scenes.title: Why incomplete blocks?
body: A complete block contains all v treatments. When a block cannot accommodate every treatment, an incomplete block contains k treatments, with k<v.
A BIBD has equal block size k, equal replication r for each treatment, and equal pair concurrence λ for every distinct pair.

items.ask: What makes a block design incomplete?
items.recall: Each block contains fewer than all treatments: k<v.
refresh: A complete block contains all v treatments.

scenes.title: The five BIBD parameters
body: v is treatments; b is blocks; r is blocks containing each treatment; k is treatments per block; λ is blocks containing each pair.
These parameters describe treatment, block and pair counts.

scenario.teaser: A trial has five varieties and blocks of size three.
scenario.title: Translate the design into symbols
body: There are v=5 varieties, b=10 blocks, k=3 varieties per block, r=6 appearances per variety, and λ=3 blocks per pair.
λ refers to a pair, not a single variety.
scenario.q: Which parameter counts blocks containing a fixed pair?

ask.q: A treatment occurs in six blocks. Which parameter is six?

blocks.body: b blocks with k treatments each give bk placements.
v treatments appearing r times each give vr placements. Hence bk=vr.
If totals differ, the parameters cannot describe a BIBD. This does not check pair balance.

ask.nudge: Count the 1s in N by columns and rows.

scenes.title: Find a missing replication
scenes.problem: A design has v=7, b=14 and k=3. Find r.
scenes.answer: Each treatment appears in six blocks.

blocks.body: It appears in r blocks, with k−1 other treatments in each: r(k−1) co-occurrence counts.
There are v−1 other treatments, each paired with it λ times: λ(v−1). Equate the counts.
λ counts shared blocks for a pair; r counts blocks for one treatment.

scenes.title: Solve λ and b
scenes.problem: Let v=6,r=5,k=3. Determine λ and b.

scenes.title: Construct the incidence matrix
body: Define N as a v×b binary matrix. Rows are treatments; columns are blocks. Nᵢⱼ=1 if treatment i occurs in block j.
Each row sums to r; each column sums to k. Total ones=vr=bk.

scenario.teaser: Four treatments are arranged in six pair-blocks.
scenario.title: Read the incidence matrix
body: Take blocks 12,13,14,23,24,34. Four rows represent treatments and six columns represent blocks.
Each row sums to three and each column to two.
scenario.q: What are the dimensions of N?

ask.q: What does each column sum equal?

scenes.title: Worked BIBD with four treatments

solution.math: Every row sums to 3, so r=3; every column to 2, so k=2.
Every pair occurs once, so λ=1. NN′ has diagonal 3 and off-diagonal 1: NN′=2I₄+J₄.

scenes.check: There are 12 ones; each pair occurs once.

ask.q: What are diagonal and off-diagonal entries of NN′?

blocks.body: The (i,i) entry is a row's dot product with itself, equal to r.
For i≠j, the dot product counts blocks containing both treatments, equal to λ.
A matrix with diagonal r and off-diagonal λ is (r−λ)I_v+λJ_v.

ask.q: What does an off-diagonal entry of NN′ represent?
ask.nudge: Common blocks for two distinct treatments.

scenes.title: Necessary conditions are not existence proofs

blocks.body: A nontrivial BIBD must satisfy positive integer parameters, k<v, bk=vr and λ(v−1)=r(k−1).
Passing these equations does not automatically prove a design exists. A construction or existence theorem may be needed.

ask.q: Do the two identities alone prove that a BIBD exists?

scenes.title: Diagnose a parameter interpretation
scenes.problem: A student says λ=2 means each treatment appears in two blocks for v=7,b=14,r=6,k=3,λ=2.

solution.math: r=6 counts blocks containing one treatment; λ=2 counts blocks containing a pair.

scenes.answer: The parameters pass both arithmetic checks, but λ was misinterpreted.
scenes.check: r is individual replication; λ is pair concurrence.

ask.q: Which parameter counts blocks containing one treatment?

scenes.title: Common BIBD examination traps
scenes.objective: Avoid symbol swaps and false existence claims.

traps.q: If k=v, is the design incomplete?
Does λ count blocks containing one treatment?
traps.a: No; r does. λ is for a pair.
No; they are necessary, not sufficient.

traps.q: If treatments are rows, what is N's size?

scenes.title: A second parameter calculation
scenes.problem: A candidate has v=9,k=3,r=4. Find λ and b.

scenes.title: BIBD mastery checkpoint
body: Remember v treatments, b blocks, r replications, k block size and λ pair concurrence.
Check bk=vr and λ(v−1)=r(k−1). For treatment-row N, row sums are r, column sums k and NN′=(r−λ)I+λJ. Feasibility is not proof of existence.
